content:
The image shows a bunch of green bananas with dark brown to black necrotic rot at the distal (tip/blossom) end of each finger. The affected tissue is dry and shrunken, resembling the burnt end of a cigar. The rest of the fruit remains green and intact.

**Evidence mapping:**
- Affected part: banana fruit tips (blossom end)
- Visual features: dry, dark brown-black necrosis confined to the tip of each finger, no leaf symptoms
- Panama Disease: causes vascular discoloration and leaf wilting, not fruit tip rot
- Yellow/Black Sigatoka: leaf disease, no fruit symptoms
- Bunchy Top: viral, stunts leaves at crown
- Cordana Leaf Spot: affects leaves only
- Cigar End Rot: classic presentation is exactly this — dry, dark necrosis at the blossom end of banana fingers, resembling a cigar tip
